metadata.description: Two-hop math reasoning questions requiring an intermediate computation step before reaching the final answer
metadata.format: Each question requires exactly two reasoning hops: (1) derive an intermediate value, (2) use it to compute the final answer

questions.question: A store sells apples for $2 each. Sarah buys 5 apples and pays with a $20 bill. How much change does she receive?

hop_1.description: How much does Sarah pay in total for 5 apples at $2 each?

questions.question: A car travels at 60 mph for 2 hours, then at 40 mph for 3 hours. What is the total distance traveled?

hop_1.description: How far does the car travel in each individual segment?

questions.question: A rectangle has length 8 cm and width 5 cm. If both dimensions are doubled, what is the area of the new rectangle?

hop_1.description: What are the new length and width after doubling each dimension?

questions.question: A bookstore has 3 shelves, each holding 12 books. After selling 15 books, how many books remain?

hop_1.description: How many books are on all 3 shelves combined?

questions.question: Tom earns $15 per hour and works 8 hours a day. If he saves 30% of his daily earnings, how much does he save per day?

hop_1.description: How much does Tom earn in one full day of work?

questions.question: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Three people each eat 2 slices. What fraction of the pizza remains?

hop_1.description: How many slices do the three people eat in total?

questions.question: Train A leaves a station at 9:00 AM at 80 km/h. Train B leaves the same station at 10:00 AM at 100 km/h in the same direction. At what time does Train B catch Train A?

hop_1.description: How far ahead is Train A when Train B departs at 10:00 AM?

hop_2.description: Compute catch-up time using relative speed

questions.question: A school has 240 students. 40% are in grade 6, and half of the grade 6 students participate in sports. How many grade 6 students participate in sports?

hop_1.description: How many of the 240 students are in grade 6?

questions.question: A tank holds 500 liters and is currently 60% full. After adding 50 liters, what percentage of the tank is filled?

hop_1.description: How many liters are in the tank after adding 50 liters to the current amount?

questions.question: A worker produces 45 items per hour. After a 20% efficiency improvement, how many items does the worker produce in an 8-hour shift?

hop_1.description: What is the worker's new hourly production rate after the 20% efficiency improvement?

questions.question: A 120-liter solution is 25% salt. If 30 liters of water evaporate and no salt is lost, what percentage of the remaining solution is salt?

hop_1.description: How many liters of salt are in the solution before evaporation?

hop_2.description: Compute the new salt percentage after 30 liters of water evaporate

questions.question: A contractor buys 250 tiles. During installation, 12% of the tiles break. Of the remaining tiles, 3/5 are used for the kitchen, and the rest are split equally between two bathrooms. How many tiles go into each bathroom?

hop_1.description: How many tiles remain after 12% break, and how many are left after using 3/5 of those remaining tiles for the kitchen?
hop_1.computation: Broken tiles = 250 × 0.12 = 30; remaining after breakage = 250 − 30 = 220; kitchen uses 220 × 3/5 = 132; tiles left for bathrooms = 220 − 132 = 88

hop_2.description: Split the remaining tiles equally between the two bathrooms
